key_insight: A self-supervised Transformer can turn variable plasma protein panels into a fixed participant representation, letting disease risk models work even when many proteins are missing.
clinical_relevance: This could make proteomic risk prediction more portable across cohorts and assay setups, improving reuse of models in real-world research settings.
method: Pretrained a protein-token Transformer with masked-protein reconstruction on 53,014 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project participants.
Generated participant-level proteomic representations from available proteins without imputing missing ones.
Tested disease prediction across 144 diseases using comprehensive 2,920-protein profiles versus partial 1,460-protein coverage.
evidence_signal: Across 144 diseases, median AUC was 0.679 with full protein coverage, 0.637 when reusing models on partial coverage without refitting, and 0.673 after retraining disease-specific models.
watch_item: Performance varied by disease group, so external validation is needed before deploying these representations across new cohorts or clinical settings.
paper_title: Self-supervised plasma proteomic representations for prospective disease prediction across varying protein availability
